newsitem.title: CANADA: Sun buyers want to keep Financial Post.
newsitem.headline: Sun buyers want to keep Financial Post.

text.p: The management group poised to complete a buyout of the Toronto Sun Publishing Corp. on Tuesday said it wants to keep the company's majority stake in the Financial Post daily business newspaper.

The Toronto Sun's chief financial officer, Bruce Jackson, said that despite news reports to the contrary the management group has not received an offer for the Financial Post from media mogul Conrad Black.
Black's Hollinger Inc., which has a controlling stake in Southam Inc., holds about 20 percent of the Financial Post.
A Canadian Press news agency report late Thursday said Southam had made an offer for the Toronto Sun's 60.2 percent holding in the Financial Post.
"We don't have any offer for the Financial Post," Jackson said in a telephone interview, referring to the report.
But he added, "Southam was in the (Toronto Sun) data room back in June or July...I believe they made an offer at that time for the Financial Post. And I think obviously there is interest there."

The report of a Southam offer came as the final days ticked away ahead of Tuesday's vote by shareholders on the management group's C$16 ($12) per share bid for Toronto Sun. The management group buyout will cost about C$411 million ($301 million), before expenses.
Toronto Sun owns a chain of tabloids in several major Canadian cities as well as the Financial Post stake.
Debt-ridden Rogers Communications Inc. in May put its 63-percent holding in Toronto Sun on the block, which led to the takeover offer for the whole company.
Jackson said despite the hefty long-term debtload the management group buyout will place on Toronto Sun, the group would prefer to keep the Financial Post.
"The Financial Post has a lot of upside to it. We believe it's got a really good future," Jackson said.
Canadian Press quoted David Radler, Southam's associate chief executive and president of Hollinger, as saying he did not know if Southam's offer for the Post would succeed.
"It's in the hands of (Toronto Sun President Paul) Godfrey," Canadian Press quoted Radler as saying.

Unless an 11th-hour offer materialises, Tuesday's vote will rubber-stamp the ownership transfer of Toronto Sun to the Godfrey-led management group, which will then be in full control of the Financial Post's future.
